question_stem:
A person uses a trolley to move suitcases at an airport. The total mass of the trolley and suitcases
is 72 kg.
question_stem_latex:
A person uses a trolley to move suitcases at an airport. The total mass of the trolley and suitcases
is 72 kg.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
The person pushes the trolley and suitcases along a horizontal surface with a constant speed
of 1.4 m s⁻¹ and then releases the trolley. The released trolley moves in a straight line and
comes to rest. Assume that a constant total resistive force of 18 N opposes the motion of the
trolley and suitcases.
parts.question_text_latex:
The person pushes the trolley and suitcases along a horizontal surface with a constant speed
of 1.4 m $s^{-1}$ and then releases the trolley. The released trolley moves in a straight line and
comes to rest. Assume that a constant total resistive force of 18 N opposes the motion of the
trolley and suitcases.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the power required to overcome the total resistive force on the trolley and
suitcases when they move with a constant speed of 1.4 m s⁻¹.
power = W
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the power required to overcome the total resistive force on the trolley and
suitcases when they move with a constant speed of 1.4 m $s^{-1}$.
$power = W $

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the time taken for the trolley to come to rest after it is released.
time = s
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the time taken for the trolley to come to rest after it is released.
$time = s $

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
At another place in the airport, the trolley and suitcases are on a slope, as shown in Fig. 2.1.
The person releases the trolley from rest at point X. The trolley moves down the slope in a
straight line towards point Y. The distance along the slope between points X and Y is 9.5 m.
The component F of the weight of the trolley and suitcases that acts along the slope is 54 N.
Assume that a constant total resistive force of 18 N opposes the motion of the trolley and
suitcases.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the speed of the trolley at point Y.
speed = m s⁻¹
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the speed of the trolley at point Y.
$speed = m s^{-1} $

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the work done by F for the movement of the trolley from X to Y.
work done = J
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the work done by F for the movement of the trolley from X to Y.
$work done = J $

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.question_text:
The trolley is released at point X at time t = 0.
On Fig. 2.2, sketch a graph to show the variation with time t of the work done by F for the
movement of the trolley from X to Y.
Numerical values of the work done and t are not required.
parts.question_text_latex:
The trolley is released at point X at time $t = 0$.
On Fig. 2.2, sketch a graph to show the variation with time $t$ of the work done by $F$ for the
movement of the trolley from X to Y.
Numerical values of the work done and $t$ are not required.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
The angle of the slope in (b) is constant. The frictional forces acting on the wheels of the
moving trolley are also constant.
Explain why, in practice, it is incorrect to assume that the total resistive force opposing the
motion of the trolley and suitcases is constant as the trolley moves between X and Y.
